name: Ui_Part_GetAnimState
signature: bool Ui_Part_GetAnimState(Ui_Part* self, AnimRecord* record, u32 arg3)
summary: Classifies how one animation record relates to this UI part and returns a state 0-5 (5 = record has no id, 4 = record forces a slot, 2 = already playing, 3 = the slot id is in the part's own slot list, else 0/1 from the condition check).
evidence: Now named callers use the return value as a state, not a boolean: Ui_Part_UpdateAnimState and Ui_Part_ReleaseAndPlay switch on it and Ui_Part_GetAnimSlotMask (0x00646ACC) tests exactly states 2/3/5. An 'Update'/'Setup' family around one part object confirms the Part attribution; only the word order changed, the guess was right.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_TestAnimRecord
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Part_TestAnimRecord(UiPart* self, AnimRecord* record, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Per-record test (not a list search): when the anim record is marked active it returns whether the member's current action state differs from the record's id, i.e. whether this record still needs to be played for that member.
evidence: Old name said Find...InList but the body takes a single record and returns a 0/1 predicate; it reuses the same record test as Ui_Part_FindAnimRecord (0x00645FB8) and is called from Ui_Part_SetupFromAnimRecord and Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand. Renamed for what it does; still maybe_ because 0x00629348 (the action-state compare) is unnamed.

name: Ui_Part_GetAnimSlotMask
signature: u32 Ui_Part_GetAnimSlotMask(Ui_Part* self, AnimRecord* record, int includeState3, u32 arg4)
summary: Builds a 6-bit mask of the animation slots the current record can use: for each of the record's six slot indices present in the part's own record array it asks Ui_Part_GetAnimState and sets the bit for states 2/5 (and 3 when includeState3 is set).
evidence: Its only real caller family is Ui_Part_SetupFromAnimRecord / Ui_MessagePage_Build, which store the mask in the part object; the per-slot helper it calls is now confirmed as Ui_Part_GetAnimState. Confirms the old name.

name: Ui_Part_FindAnimRecord
signature: u32 Ui_Part_FindAnimRecord(UiPart* self, u32 animId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Searches the part's 0x1c-byte animation records for the one whose u16 id at +8 equals animId, and when that record is active also requires the member's action state to differ (0x00629348).
evidence: Sits in the confirmed Ui_Part_* animation family (Ui_Part_SetupFromAnimRecord, Ui_Part_GetAnimSlotMask) and is the array-search version of the single-record test 0x00646060, so 'find the record' is right.

name: Actor_CheckVisibleFlags
signature: int Actor_CheckVisibleFlags(Actor* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Decides whether an actor may currently be shown/handled: asks the actor's sub-object (vtable +0x48 then +0x18), otherwise combines the actor flags at +0x4E1 and +0x1385, and when Work byte 0x27C57 is set additionally requires the actor id to pass the lookups 0x00669DD4/0x00669E24.
evidence: Seven battle action-state updaters (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateActionState/Composite/Pose/Motion/AuraState) call it as a gate on the returned 0/1, which supports 'visible/handled' rather than a getter. Still called Check... because which flag decides visibility is not proven.

name: Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow
signature: void* Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow(UiItemRef* ref, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves a UI list item reference {index, kind} to its row record: kind 0 -> the work's bag rows (work+0x24a98+0x5fe4, stride 0x8c), kind 1 -> the external list at *g_00630994+0x6b8 (stride 0x98), kind 2 -> the table at +0x7b3c (stride 0x8c, 20 rows).
evidence: Confirmed callers Ui_SpriteList_LoadPage/Ui_SpriteList_LoadPageEx and Ui_TenRowTextWindow_FillRows all pass a row reference and use the result as the row record; the sibling 0x00630998 is the same resolver without the kind switch.

name: maybe_Ui_MemberTable_Init
summary: Lazily creates three per-member tables (member count < 8) in the bag work and fills them from the character records; sits in the equip-window code block and is called from 0x004ABC48.
evidence: Old name claimed a party status panel, but the body touches no window/panel object at all: it allocates 0x24-byte-per-member tables guarded by 0x007BE30C/0x007BE310 and fills them via func_00640164 / maybe_Party_GetMemberCount. Its named caller block is Ui_EquipWindow_* (Ui_EquipWindow_BindMessagePanes is the function right before it), so the status-panel attribution had no support.

name: maybe_Ui_TenRowWindow_BuildRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_TenRowWindow_BuildRows(ScrollBar* self, DrawObject* templ, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 extra)
summary: Builds a ten-row paged list: creates the 'null_txt_l0'..'null_txt_l9' text panes and 'icon_ex0'..'icon_ex9' icons row by row, then the 'pager_num_l'/'pager_num_r'/'txt_title' panes, and finally sorts the row byte table at self+0x22..0x79 with the app's sort comparator.
evidence: Body reads the literals 'null_txt_l0', 'icon_ex0', 'pager_num_r', 'pager_num_l', 'txt_title' and creates exactly ten rows before the pager setup; nothing scroll-bar specific. Old name was wrong about the class, but which window class it is (message/log list vs shop) is not proven, so maybe_.

name: Battle_ActionAnimTable_FindEntry
summary: Finds the action-animation table row for the current member: job byte (func_005B0C6C) + second id (func_00384B6C) are matched against 0x20-byte records with wildcard 0xFF job/category bytes and two optional flag ids (Work+0x2A444 bitmap, Work+0x27508 bytes).
evidence: Confirmed caller Battle_ActionAnimTable_InitSlots plus the sibling maybe_Battle_ActionAnimTable_GetMode/Release make this a lookup on the same lazily built table object (guard 0x007BE33C).

name: maybe_Ui_StoryTable_FindEntry
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_StoryTable_FindEntry(WorkData* self, u32 packedTableId, u32 packedKey, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up a 0x28-byte row by three packed keys (+0x20 u16, +0x22 u16, +0x24 u8) in the sub-table selected by the low byte of the id, falling back to per-member work data (work+0x24a98) when the id is below 0x36.
evidence: Both confident callers are the story/memoir (senreki) windows: Ui_StoryListWindow_BindRowModels and Ui_StoryPanel_SetupRecord, which read story ids from Work+0x2A49C. Nothing in the body deals with rewards or drops, so the old 'reward' wording was unsupported; the table identity itself is still inferred from its callers.

name: Text_InvokeControlHandler
signature: void Text_InvokeControlHandler(TextControl* self, u16 ownerId, u16* text, u32 arg4)
summary: Dispatches one text control code: resolves the string (0x0066CCEC), binds the owner member into the shared text builder, appends the control character, flushes it and jumps through the per-code handler table g_00641F78 indexed by self+4.
evidence: Named callees Text_Layout_RunPass and Text_SetFormatArgsFromPlayerData tie it to the text formatter, and the handler-table jump explains the void return. Old guess holds.

name: Ui_Part_BuildAnimSlotList
signature: void Ui_Part_BuildAnimSlotList(u8* out, Ui_PartList* list, u32 groupId)
summary: Fills a 7-entry list with the slot ids (+0x19) of the part-list records that belong to the requested group and whose 0x1c record is used by at least one list entry.
evidence: Confirmed caller Ui_MessagePage_Build uses the produced slot list to set up the message part table; the record fields match the Ui_Part family (0x1c records, func_00672364 init).

name: maybe_Ui_Part_GetRemainingAnimTime
summary: Returns the part's total animation duration (0x00629280) minus the duration of every slot whose u16 entry at +0xa0 resolves to a record (0x0063CF74), i.e. the time left to play.
evidence: No named caller or callee pins it further (Ui_SkillPanel_HandleInput is itself an unverified name at 0x0036DF38); the arithmetic (total - already-played) is clear, the 'remaining' framing stays a guess.

name: Ui_Equip_GetEquippedItemId
signature: u32 Ui_Equip_GetEquippedItemId(UiBagList* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the item id currently equipped in one equipment slot of a member (func_006292F0), or the default constant g_0064C464 when the member id or the column (< 6) is invalid.
evidence: Confident callers Ui_EquipWindow_HandleInput and Ui_EquipWindow_InitPanes read it to show/compare equipment; the callee func_006292F0 is the known 'equipped item id in slot' helper (FACTS.md), so it is not a bag list and not a selected-row getter. Renamed accordingly.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchA
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchA(UiRow* row, u32 paneId, u16* entry, u32 stack)
summary: Row renderer variant A: resolves the list entry (0x0066C5CC), copies it into the shared 0x3C0-byte row buffer, sets the pane colours, flushes the pane and tail-dispatches through the row-kind handler table indexed by row+4.
evidence: Only self-references in the readable tree; the three A/B/C variants differ only in the entry source and filter byte, so the shared wording is kept. Kind table contents unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchB
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchB(UiRow* row, u32 paneId, u16* entry, u32 stack)
summary: Row renderer variant B: skips rows whose sub-record kind byte (+0x29) does not match the row's filter, then copies the entry into the shared row buffer, flushes the pane and dispatches through the table at 0x00652794.
evidence: Still no named caller (the only reference is its own address in the A/B/C family). Summary sharpened with the filter byte, name unchanged.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchC
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawDispatchC(UiRow* row, u32 paneId, u16* entry, u32 stack)
summary: Row renderer variant C (724 bytes): draws only entries whose sub-record kind equals the row filter byte at +5, submits with the alternate/selected flag 1 to 0x0045A5A0 and dispatches through the table at 0x00652854.
evidence: Same unnamed A/B/C family, no named caller; the body confirms the kind filter and the 'selected' submission flag, so only the summary changed.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_BuildSortedEntryIds
summary: Fills the window's up-to-32-entry u16 table with (type, id) pairs gathered from two resolvers (type 1 when the record has +0x80 bit0, type 2 when +0x2E9 bit0), stores the count, sorts the pairs with a dedicated comparator (std_introsort_u16_fnptr) and notifies the window.
evidence: Called only through the window vtable, so the named-caller check adds nothing; the sort + notify structure matches the old name but the window class stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_ResetLargeScreenState
summary: Resets a large (0x4400+ byte) screen object: rebuilds the 8-entry table at +0x11C, resolves the view at +0x148, lazily creates the 0x80-byte helper, then (when 0x00383A80 says the scene is active) empties the element list at +0x300, frees cached nodes, resets three list heads, rebinds +0x43E0 and sets the animator to state 0.
evidence: Only Ui_GetCore and Game_GetWork are named around it; 'large screen' is still the only support for the name, so kept maybe_ with a fuller summary.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileWindow_RefreshStats
summary: Refreshes the value panes of a profile card: formats play time and the per-title counters, binds the matching icons and writes the icon of the currently selected title.
evidence: Callers/callees are unnamed (0066B2CC/0066B45C/0066B5F8, 0063CC1C/0063CD18); 'profile window' remains a guess from the title/play-time strings, so kept.

name: maybe_Ui_GridWindow_SetCompareMark
signature: void maybe_Ui_GridWindow_SetCompareMark(UiGridWindow* self, ItemId item, int mark)
summary: Picks the up/down/same comparison icon for the given item (honouring the current sort direction) and writes it into pane |0xb.
evidence: No named caller; body only reaches Game_GetWork/Ui_GetCore and 0x00633560, so the 'compare mark' meaning rests entirely on the icon selection, unchanged.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitStateB
summary: Second initialiser of the 0x4AC000 state table: bails out when the mode byte says the screen is already prepared, otherwise allocates/grows the table through 0x0011FE8C/0x0011CFAC and initialises the 0x80-byte helper (0x00384050).
evidence: Only named caller is Field_SetupTalkParams, which undermines the casino attribution; the allocation pattern is identical to 0x004ABC48, so both stay maybe_ with the same word.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_OpenResultPage
summary: Opens the result page of the uma (horse-race) window: mode 3 selects states 8/7, mode 4 states 9/7; sets message arguments #5 (member name id) and #6 (selection value) via Message_SetArg and starts the sub-window with that state.
evidence: Message_SetArg is the only named callee; the mode->state mapping is clear but nothing names the window class, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_NumberPane_SetIconAndText
summary: Refreshes a number pane: takes the counter from the shared font/text object, applies it to the pane's text handle and sets the string from text id 0x1F.
evidence: Only Ui_GetCore/Game_GetWork and 0x00707C1C are named here; the two actions (count + text id) fit the name, but no caller confirms the pane class.

name: maybe_Ui_CriticalPopup_InitTitle
summary: Initialises the popup title row: pane 0 gets the 'txt_title' label with animation id 0x2E, the second text object goes to pane 1, then the icon (0x2F or 0x30) is chosen from bit 0 of the story flag byte Work+0x2D384.
evidence: No named caller or callee; 'critical popup' rests on the animation ids alone, so kept maybe_ with the flag byte spelled out.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyWorkLayout
summary: Rebuilds a 0x40-byte block of sixteen layout/sprite ids from a small allocated record and installs it into the window subsystem at work+0x24a98 (via 0x00613F14).
evidence: Callers are unverified (maybe_Ui_MapWindow_RefreshEntry) and the body only names Game_GetWork/Game_GetDataManager; kept.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_HasTextOverride
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ListRow_HasTextOverride(UiListModel* self, u16 rowId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns 1 when the row has an entry with a non-null string that is not currently overridden, i.e. whether a script-supplied label exists for this row.
evidence: New context is only the poker-window family (Ui_PokerWindow_Payout, maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_BindCardText), which uses it as a per-row label test but does not name the list model; kept.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetTextPixelWidth
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetTextPixelWidth(UiListModel* self, int row, u32 third)
summary: Estimates the pixel width of a row label: resolves the row's text id (model table or global list 0x0063DD38), measures it and returns min(width, 9).
evidence: Callers Ui_PokerWindow_Confirm/HandlePayout use it for layout only; nothing confirms the 'list row' model, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Party_GetMemberName
signature: int maybe_Party_GetMemberName(u32 arg1, int memberIndex, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns a pointer to the given party member's name field: active-member data from the party scanner plus 0xCA, which is the 7-character name field of the member record (no bounds check).
evidence: Named callee is Party_GetActiveMemberDataByIndex and FACTS.md records the party-member name at +0xCA (7 chars). The callers are list text builders (Ui_ListText_GetTextForSlot, maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel) that use it as the row's display label, so 'name' fits better than 'actor data block'. The twin 0x0063A87C has the identical body.

name: maybe_Actor_SetBagSlotId
signature: void maybe_Actor_SetBagSlotId(Actor* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Publishes the actor's u16 id at +0x2B8 into the work's row/registry table through the unnamed setter 0x0066B3B0.
evidence: Named caller IsThereGimmickFixedItem calls it right where it checks for a fixed/gimmick item, which fits publishing an id to the work table, but neither the callee 0x0066B3B0 nor the +0x2B8 field is named, so 'bag slot' stays a guess.

name: maybe_Actor_SetSecondBagSlotId
signature: void maybe_Actor_SetSecondBagSlotId(Actor* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Same publish-to-work helper as 0x00640D08 but reads the actor's second u16 id at +0x2EC (276 bytes: also validates the value first).
evidence: Identical body to 0x00640D08 apart from the field; same unnamed work setter and the same IsThereGimmickFixedItem caller. Nothing new names the field, so kept.

name: maybe_Item_GetCountThresholdTag
signature: u32 maybe_Item_GetCountThresholdTag(CounterList* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Walks the 4-byte {count, u16 id} list at self+0x20 and returns the id of the first entry whose count exceeds the value read at g_00643904+ctx, or the default g_00643908 when none does.
evidence: Callers are all in the guide/help window family (Ui_GuideWindow_Update, maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_CheckTextFits/LayoutPage), which explains the count threshold but not the 'Item' in the name; kept with the threshold rule spelled out.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_CountMatchingParts
summary: Counts how many of the animation record's six slot bytes (+0x54..+0x59) match one of the member's current animation ids (0x006298D0), i.e. how many sub-parts this record affects.
evidence: No named caller; the loop is unambiguous but the 'part' terminology is inherited from the Ui_Part family, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_LoadWorkData
summary: Applies one stored work record to the live game: validates the inventory (0x0064C8E8), applies the record (0x0064CB24), replays the pending HP deltas, resets the actor lists, then re-applies the five saved equipment ids (self+0x2C.., only when < 100) and the trailing u16 id list.
evidence: Named callee Text_AdvanceTyping is incidental; the callers (maybe_Ui_Window_RebuildItemTextAndStartLoad/SetLabelFromSelection) suggest a load/refresh path, and 'save' is still only inferred from the record struct.

name: maybe_Party_MemberFlagPairA
summary: Tests one of two member flag pairs, selecting the pair from the global switch bytes Work+0x27C5A/0x27C5B (0x10|0x1000 or 0x20|0x800) and returning whether any of the chosen bits is set in member+0x74.
evidence: Named caller Camera_UpdateManualYaw uses it as a member-group test, which does not resolve which group the bits mean; it is the exact complement of 0x0066A660 (same switch bytes), so the pair naming is kept.

name: maybe_Party_MemberFlagPairB
summary: Complement of 0x0066A604: tests the other member flag pair (0x20|0x800 or 0x10|0x1000, chosen by the same two global bytes) on member+0x74, i.e. 'is this member in the other group'.
evidence: Same evidence as its complement; the only named caller is Camera_UpdateManualYaw, so the group semantics remain unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_SetResultFlags
signature: void maybe_Ui_SetResultFlags(u32 arg1, u32 mode, int value)
summary: Message-window result hook: when maybe_Message_GetWindowMode(arg1) is non-zero it installs handlers 1 and 2 on the window block at arg1+0x228 and sets the per-save byte root+0x2D303 to 1.
evidence: Body is damaged (bad-instruction truncation), so only the two handler installs and the 0x2D303 byte are trustworthy; named callee maybe_Message_GetWindowMode hints at the message window but 'result flags' is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateA
summary: Table-dispatched wrapper: reads one word from the global context and the map-state value from 0x0066BAC4(work+0x24a98) and passes both to maybe_Ui_FourRowList_Reset.
evidence: Its only real callee is the (still maybe_) four-row reset; the named-looking callers (maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance3) are unverified. Twin of 0x003F7290, kept.

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateB
summary: Second wrapper around the same four-row reset: identical body to 0x003F6F20, using context offset 0x003F72CC and the map-state getter 0x0066BA6C instead of 0x0066BAC4.
evidence: Byte-for-byte twin of 0x003F6F20 except for two constants; nothing named confirms who dispatches it, so kept.

name: maybe_Field_NotifyActor
signature: void maybe_Field_NotifyActor(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Forwards an actor id plus two payload words to the field/actor manager at work+0x24a98 (0x005BCA28(id, manager, ...)), 44 bytes with no other work.
evidence: No named caller or callee exists (0x005BCA28 is unnamed), so the event meaning of the payload is unrecoverable; kept.

name: maybe_Field_LoadAreaActorData
summary: Searches the current map's actor/object tables for areaId, caches the matching 0x28-byte record in the work cache words, then rebuilds the per-cell actor entries for 0x36 map cells with 9 sub-slots each.
evidence: 1384 bytes with no direct caller (table-dispatched); named callees are only Game_GetWork/Game_GetDataManager, so 'load area actor data' remains a description of the loops rather than proof.

name: maybe_Field_IsEventMode
summary: Returns 1 when the per-world byte at g_0014FF44 has bit 0x80 CLEAR and the map-mode query (0x0066B17C on work+0x24a98) returns <= 0x0E; i.e. 'normal field play', not 'in event' - the name reads the opposite way.
evidence: Named caller Ui_MessageWindow_SelectRowStyle / Ui_Window_WaitAndStartTransition use it as a 'normal field' gate. The polarity is now documented, but the mode range 0..0x0E is not decoded, so the name is kept (and flagged as inverted in the summary).

name: maybe_Actor_AddField14
summary: Resolves the party-member record and adds delta to its stat field at +0x14 through the record's first virtual setter (vtable slot 0).
evidence: Callee is the known member-record helper 0x0035EB98 and the counterpart getters/setters (0x0015E7A0, 0x00152D5C) use the same field; which stat +0x14 is remains unknown, so kept.

name: maybe_Actor_AddClampedValue
summary: Adds delta to the member's current value at +0x16 and clamps it to the maximum stored at +0x12.
evidence: The clamp pair +0x12/+0x16 is read by the getters 0x0015858C/0x0015E7D0 and written absolutely by 0x00152D98; a current/max pair like HP is likely but not proven from the record layout, so kept.

name: maybe_Work_GetGold
summary: Tail-call getter: returns 0x0066B2CC(bagWork, 0), i.e. entry 0 of the u32 counter array at bag+0x31F4. Entry 0 is the money the amount spinner checks against the 9,999,999 gold cap, so this is the wallet/gold getter; the other entries of the array are other counters.
evidence: Disassembly: `push {r3,lr}; mov r0,sp; bl 0x6F20C0; ldr r0,[r0]; mov r1,#0; add r0,#0x24A98; bl 0x66B2CC; pop {r3,pc}` - the callee's r0 survives, so Ghidra's void typing dropped a return value (FACTS: getter trap). The old name 'SetModeFlag' was the opposite of what happens. 0x0066B2CC is 3 instructions (`work[index*4+0x31F4]`) and 0x003D28FC clamps its entry 0 against 0x0098967F (the gold cap), which is why entry 0 is read as gold.

name: maybe_Actor_SetFieldViaVtable
summary: Resolves the party-member record and stores value through its first virtual setter (the same slot the add-helper uses).
evidence: Same vtable slot as maybe_Actor_AddField14 (0x00150D48), which confirms it is a stat setter but not which stat; kept.

name: maybe_Actor_SetClampedValue
summary: Sets the member's current value at +0x16 to value, clamped to the maximum at +0x12.
evidence: Absolute-set counterpart of 0x00150D8C with the same +0x12/+0x16 pair; field identity still unproven, kept.

name: maybe_Field_SetModeByte
summary: Stores a single mode byte in the field manager at work+0x27C7B (52 bytes).
evidence: No callers and no named callee; only the destination byte is known, so kept.

name: maybe_Field_CheckPositionAndTrigger
signature: void maybe_Field_CheckPositionAndTrigger(u32 x, u32 y, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Compares the current map position with (x,y) (20.12 packed coordinates, high halves) and on a match forwards the trigger parameters to 0x0035F0C4 with mode 1.
evidence: The coordinate comparison is clear but both 0x0035F0C4 and 0x0066B5F8 are unnamed and there are no callers, so kept. The predicate-looking name is harmless here: the body performs the trigger as a side effect and returns no value (no return register is set), so the dropped-return trap does not apply. (checked: predicate-name flag does not apply).

name: maybe_Actor_InvokeVtable1
summary: Resolves the party-member record and invokes its second virtual method (slot 1) with no arguments, i.e. a no-arg update/reset.
evidence: Nothing named around it; the vtable entry index is the only fact, so kept.

name: maybe_Actor_GetMaxValue
summary: Returns the member's maximum value field at +0x12 (the clamp used by 0x00150D8C/0x00152D98).
evidence: Consistent with the add/set clamp pair, but which stat it is stays unknown; kept.

name: maybe_Field_SetStat
summary: Guarded field-manager write: when not in event mode, stores value in the per-index stat array (final store is `str r2,[r0 + r1*4 + 0x2998]` in 0x00612B08) and pokes 0x00612B08's companion query.
evidence: Disassembly of the callee confirms a per-index slot, but neither the index space nor the stat meaning is known; kept.

name: maybe_Field_SetFlagBit
summary: Sets bit 0 of the per-index flag byte at work+0x5762+index (reads, ORs 1, writes back).
evidence: Callee 0x00612550 unnamed, no callers; likely a visited/enabled flag but unproven, kept.

name: maybe_Actor_GetField14
summary: Returns the member's stat field at +0x14 (the value 0x00150D48 adds to).
evidence: Paired with the add-helper through the same vtable field; stat identity unknown, kept.

name: maybe_Actor_GetField16
summary: Returns the member's current value at +0x16 (the field clamped by the maximum at +0x12).
evidence: Same clamp pair as 0x00150D8C/0x00152D98; kept.

name: maybe_Field_SetState
summary: Writes a state value into the field manager through 0x0066B004 (40 bytes).
evidence: Callee unnamed, no callers; only that it writes a state word is certain, kept.

name: maybe_Party_SpendResource
summary: Spends up to amount of a party resource: reads the current value of stat slot 10 (0x0066B0F8(world,10)) and, when it is below -amount, stores the reduced value through the per-index stat writer (0x00612B08 with index 10).
evidence: The hard-coded index 10 and the generic per-index stat array (+0x2998, same as maybe_Field_SetStat) show it is one specific counter, not a general 'resource'; no callers, so the name's wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Actor_EnsureVisible
summary: Sets actor flags through 0x00192414, special-casing the visibility bit 0x80: if bit 7 of the actor flag halfword at +0xDA is already set it does nothing.
evidence: The 0x80 fast path and the +0xDA flag word are clear, but nothing named uses it as a visibility guarantee; kept.

name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance(Dialog* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
